title: TCS Opens AI-Native Creative Studio in London as Part of 5,000-Job UK Expansion
excerpt: The 4,500-square-foot facility is TCS Interactive's second global studio after New York, bringing together designers, engineers and strategists to co-create AI-powered products for UK clients.
body:
• TCS has launched a 4,500-square-foot AI-native creative engineering studio in London under its TCS Interactive arm
  • The studio is part of TCS's commitment to create 5,000 jobs across the UK and Ireland over three years
  • It follows a similar facility opened in New York in 2025, forming a global creative engineering network
  • The launch comes alongside TCS's broader "Infrastructure-to-Intelligence" strategy, including a $7.4 billion AI data centre in Hyderabad and the €320 million acquisition of Porsche's IT consultancy MHP

London Gets a New AI Hub

Tata Consultancy Services has opened a new AI-native creative engineering studio in London, expanding the Indian IT giant's design and digital transformation capabilities in one of its most important overseas markets.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PH7u_oqTjbA

The 4,500-square-foot facility, announced on Monday through an exchange filing, will operate under TCS Interactive — the company's digital design, marketing and experience-led transformation arm. It is the second such studio after a New York location launched in 2025, and together the two form the backbone of a global creative engineering network.

"The UK&I is a vital market for TCS, and this studio reflects our commitment to driving innovation for our clients and AI-led creative engineering."

— Vinay Singhvi, Head – UK & Ireland, TCS

What the Studio Will Do

The London hub will serve as a co-creation space where hybrid teams of designers, strategists, domain experts and engineers work alongside clients. The focus is on turning AI concepts into commercial products, with applications spanning customer experience design, brand strategy, product development and operational efficiency.

"Our vision is to help our clients unlock new growth opportunities by orchestrating strategy, product design, engineering, and insights with an AI-led approach," said Kamal Bhadada, president of TCS Interactive. He described the London studio as sitting "at the heart of this global network" connecting UK clients to TCS's worldwide capabilities.

The facility will also act as a gateway for regional clients to access TCS's broader network of studios and technical resources across its global operations.

Part of a Bigger UK Bet

The studio opening is part of TCS's pledge to create 5,000 new jobs across the UK and Ireland over the next three years. With consolidated revenues exceeding $30 billion in the fiscal year ended March 2026, TCS is the largest Indian IT services employer in the UK.

The investment comes at a time when TCS is aggressively expanding its footprint. Days before the London announcement, its HyperVault subsidiary unveiled plans for a 1-gigawatt, up-to-$7.4 billion AI data centre campus in Hyderabad. In August, TCS agreed to acquire Porsche's IT consultancy MHP for €320 million alongside a €1.25 billion five-year services deal. Analysts at TechMarketView described the moves as part of CEO K Krithivasan's "Infrastructure-to-Intelligence" strategy to own the full stack from compute to creative.

Diaspora and Industry Implications

For Indian tech professionals in the UK, the expansion signals continued demand for AI, design and engineering talent. TCS already employs thousands of Indian-origin workers across Britain, and the 5,000-job commitment could create additional opportunities for skilled diaspora workers in a competitive market.

The studio also positions TCS against Western rivals like Accenture and Publicis Sapient in the high-margin creative engineering space, where generative AI is rapidly reducing the cost of content production but increasing the premium on fusing design with engineering expertise.

What's Next

TCS said the London studio will begin client engagements immediately. The company is expected to continue building out its global studio network as it competes for creative and AI transformation contracts across Europe and North America.
